blocks.text: Temporal is the new standard for date and time in JavaScript.
New Temporal objects were designed to replace the old Date object.

Unlike legacy Date, Temporal objects are immutable and provide first-class support for time zones,
daylight saving time, date arithmetic and non-Gregorian calendars.
Temporal reached TC39 Stage 4 in July 2026.

Stage 4 means the feature is complete and will be included in the next publication.
An important timing detail is that ECMAScript 2026 had already been cut,
and it did not contain Temporal.
Conclusion: Temporal is JavaScript 2027, not JavaScript 2026.

This can be slightly confusing because it became Stage 4 during 2026, and browsers began implementing Temporal
long before before the ES2026 release.
Temporal is a major update to the JavaScript standard.

It is currently supported in Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Opera
and is expected to reach full availability across browsers before 2027.

The Safari implementation can be tested in
Safari Technology Preview by enabling the --use-temporal runtime flag.

blocks.text: Learn why Temporal is the modern alternative to Date.
The Temporal.Duration object represents a length of time.
The Temporal.Duration object includes these properties:
years, months, weeks, days, hours, minutes, seconds, milliseconds, and nanoseconds.

The Duration object is used to perform precise date and time arithmetic (e.g. add and subtract) without
the bugs and complexity associated with the old JavaScript Date object.

blocks.text: The Temporal.Instant object represents an exact moment in UTC time.
It has NO time zone and NO calendar.
It stores nanoseconds since January 1, 1970 00:00:00 (Unix epoch).

blocks.text: The Temporal.PlainDateTime object is a pure date and time object.
It represents a calendar date and a wall-clock time with no time zone.

blocks.text: The Temporal.PlainDate object represents a calendar date without a time.
A Temporal.PlainDate is typically in ISO 8601 format (2026-05-01).

It is easier to use and safer to compare than DateTime objects for dates that are
the same regardless of time zone, such as birthdays or holidays.

blocks.text: The Temporal.PlainMonthDay() object is a month and day object.
It represents the month and day of an ISO 8601 calendar, without a year or time.
The Temporal.PlainTime object is a time object without a date.
It represents an ISO 8601 wall-clock time without a date or time zone.
It is useful for opening hours, alarms, and any time-only values.
The Temporal.ZonedDateTime object represents a date and time with a time zone.
It is the safest way to handle international date and time calculations.
It prevents common DST bugs and makes time zone conversions clear and predictable.

blocks.text: Temporal provides methods for easy and reliable date and time arithmetic.
Add and subtract days, months, years, and time without modifying the original.
Perform date arithmetic without DST bugs and Time Zone problems.
The since() method calculates the since duration between two dates.
The until() method calculates the until duration between two dates.
The since() and until() are effectivly the inverse of each other.
In JavaScript, objects cannot be compared using operators like <, >, ==, or ===.
Always use the equals() or compare() methods rather than standard equality operators.
